components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
Depicts a person standing tall, gazing up at the moon 月 — the image of looking into the distance, the source of 望's meaning 'to gaze, hope, expect.'

example.hanzi: 别指望他会来帮忙。
example.pinyin: Bié zhǐwàng tā huì lái bāngmáng.
example.english: Don't count on him coming to help.
example.fact: 指望 most often shows up in negative warnings (别指望, 不能指望) telling someone not to rely on an uncertain outcome — a more colloquial, slightly resigned register than the neutral 希望 or 期望.

meanings: have a guess! (playful, reduplicated form of 猜)

components.note: 犭 (dog) shows 猜 relates to an animal sense used metaphorically for a hunch.
青 (qīng) gives a sound distantly related to cāi, having drifted apart over time.
犭 (dog) shows 猜 relates to an animal sense used metaphorically for a hunch.
青 (qīng) gives a sound distantly related to cāi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 你猜猜这是什么礼物。
example.pinyin: Nǐ cāicai zhè shì shénme lǐwù.
example.english: Guess what this gift is.
example.fact: Reduplicating a one-syllable verb (猜 → 猜猜) softens a request into a playful invitation, the same pattern as 看看 ("take a look") and 想想 ("think it over") — the second syllable typically loses its tone in speech.

components.note: 咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
木 (wood) pictures a wooden dyeing vat.
氿-shaped strokes above picture liquid dye poured into it, giving 染 its meaning 'to dye.'

example.hanzi: 伤口感染了,需要马上看医生。
example.pinyin: Shāngkǒu gǎnrǎn le, xūyào mǎshàng kàn yīshēng.
example.english: The wound got infected — you need to see a doctor right away.
example.fact: Beyond the medical sense, 感染 extends naturally to emotions — 他的热情感染了大家 ("his enthusiasm was infectious to everyone") — much like "infectious" can describe a laugh or a mood in English.

components.note: 尤 (particularly/outstanding) — relates to 就's sense of approaching or arriving at a particular point
京 (jīng, capital) gives a sound close to 就's pronunciation jiù
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō

example.hanzi: 他明天有事,也就是说他不能来了。
example.pinyin: Tā míngtiān yǒu shì, yě jiù shì shuō tā bù néng lái le.
example.english: He has something on tomorrow — in other words, he can't come.
example.fact: 也就是说 chains together four small, ordinary words (也 "also", 就 "then", 是 "is", 说 "say") into one fixed discourse marker — a good example of how Chinese often builds transitional phrases by fusing simple pieces rather than coining a dedicated word.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows 抛 describes throwing something with the hand.
亠厶-shaped top pictures a bundled object being cast away.
廾 (two hands) below shows the act of throwing it out, giving 弃 its meaning 'to abandon, discard.'

example.hanzi: 他抛弃了自己的家人。
example.pinyin: Tā pāoqì le zìjǐ de jiārén.
example.english: He abandoned his own family.
example.fact: 抛 by itself already means "to throw, to toss," so 抛弃 reinforces it with 弃 ("to discard") — pairing two near-synonyms to intensify a verb is a common Chinese word-formation strategy.

components.note: 身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 她今年三十岁,还是单身。
example.pinyin: Tā jīnnián sānshí suì, háishi dānshēn.
example.english: She's thirty this year and still single.
example.fact: 单身 describes relationship or marital status specifically, distinct from 一个人 ("alone," a physical state) — you can be 单身 while out with a big group of friends, or 一个人 for an evening while happily in a relationship.

components.note: An altered form of 囟 (the mind/head) — the seat of thought.
心 (heart) — thinking was pictured as an activity of both mind and heart, giving 思 its meaning 'to think.'
耂 (a variant of 老, 'old') — 考 relates to careful examination and testing
丂 gives a loose sound connection to 考's reading kǎo

example.hanzi: 这个问题值得我们认真思考。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí zhídé wǒmen rènzhēn sīkǎo.
example.english: This question is worth thinking about carefully.
example.fact: 思考 pairs 思 ("to think") with 考 ("to examine, to test" — the same 考 in 考试, "exam"), giving the compound a more deliberate, analytical flavor than the everyday 想.

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
口 (mouth) — 吃 relates to eating, done with the mouth
乞 (qǐ) gives a sound close to 吃's reading chī

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的菜很好吃。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài hěn hǎochī.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is delicious.
example.fact: 好 + verb forms a whole family of evaluative adjectives this way — 好吃 (tasty), 好喝 (nice to drink), 好看 (good-looking), 好听 (nice to listen to) — each literally "good to [verb]."

components.note: 女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
十 — traditionally read as a great man standing tall.
一 (the two horizontal strokes) — heaven above and earth below, which the king bridges, giving 王 its meaning 'king, monarch.'

example.hanzi: 女王住在皇宫里。
example.pinyin: Nǚwáng zhù zài huánggōng lǐ.
example.english: The queen lives in the palace.
example.fact: 女王 (a woman who reigns as monarch in her own right) is distinct from 王后 (a king's wife) — English "queen" collapses both roles into a single word, but Chinese keeps them separate.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 趴 relates to the position of the body, legs splayed.
八 (bā) gives a sound close to 趴's reading pā, sharing the final though the initial has shifted.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: “都趴下!”警察大声喊道。
example.pinyin: “Dōu pāxia!” jǐngchá dàshēng hǎndào.
example.english: "Everybody get down!" the police shouted.
example.fact: 趴 alone already means "lying face-down," so adding the directional complement 下 ("down") highlights the motion of dropping into that position — the same 下 that turns 坐 ("sit") into 坐下 ("sit down").

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'

example.hanzi: 我们打开地图找路。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎkāi dìtú zhǎo lù.
example.english: We opened the map to find the way.
example.fact: 图 alone means "picture, chart, diagram" — the same 图 that appears in 画图 ("to draw a diagram") and 图书馆 ("library," close to "picture-book hall").

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 按 relates to pressing something with the hand
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 按's reading àn, differing only in tone
灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 请按照说明书操作。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào shuōmíngshū cāozuò.
example.english: Please operate according to the instructions.
example.fact: 按照 introduces the rule, standard, or procedure an action follows; it overlaps heavily with 根据 in meaning, though 按照 tends to lean toward following something exactly, like an instruction manual.

components.note: 羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'
女 (woman) — 妙 originally described a young woman's delicate charm, extended to mean 'wonderful, clever.'
少 (shǎo) gives a sound distantly related to miào, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 音乐会的旋律非常美妙。
example.pinyin: Yīnyuèhuì de xuánlǜ fēicháng měimiào.
example.english: The melody at the concert was truly wonderful.
example.fact: 美妙 typically describes things experienced through the senses — music, scenery, a voice — rather than a person's looks, where 美丽 or 漂亮 is used instead.

meanings: Excuse me, I must be leaving now.

components.note: 丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'
阝 (mound, place) shows 陪 relates to being present alongside someone somewhere.
咅 gives a sound distantly related to péi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我有点事,先失陪了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎn shì, xiān shīpéi le.
example.english: I have something to take care of — please excuse me for now.
example.fact: 失陪 literally means "to lose [the ability to] accompany you" (陪 = "to accompany") and survives today only as this one fixed, polite formula for excusing oneself — never as a general verb for "leaving."

meanings: (of a shop, school etc) to shut down

components.note: 门 (a door) — the frame of a doorway.
才 here representing a bar or beam laid across it, together giving 闭 its meaning 'to close, shut, block up.'

example.hanzi: 这家商店已经关闭了。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn yǐjīng guānbì le.
example.english: This shop has already shut down.
example.fact: 关闭 sounds more formal and often more permanent than the everyday 关 — you 关门 (close the door) every night, but a business, a factory, or an era of history 关闭.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 擅 describes a hand-related skill, being good at something.
亶 (dǎn) gives a sound only distantly related to shàn today, having drifted apart over time.
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 她擅长弹钢琴。
example.pinyin: Tā shàncháng tán gāngqín.
example.english: She's skilled at playing the piano.
example.fact: 擅长 takes a skill or activity directly as its object with no preposition needed (擅长 + 弹钢琴), unlike English "good at," which requires "at" before the gerund.

components.note: 予 (to give) — 幻 is drawn as an inverted, mirror-image form of 予, picturing something turned upside down or not as it seems, giving 幻 its meaning 'illusion, fantasy.'
心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢幻想自己是超级英雄。
example.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan huànxiǎng zìjǐ shì chāojí yīngxióng.
example.english: Kids like to fantasize about being superheroes.
example.fact: 幻 ("illusory, phantom") also appears in 幻觉 ("hallucination") and 科幻 ("science fiction," literally "science-fantasy") — a character reserved almost entirely for things imagined rather than real.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — many traditional medicines were made from plants and herbs
约 (yuē) gives a sound related to 药's reading yào, from an older, closer pronunciation link
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 医生给他开了一些药物。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi tā kāi le yìxiē yàowù.
example.english: The doctor prescribed him some medication.
example.fact: 药物 is the general, slightly clinical term for medicine as a category (used in pharmacology and medical reports), while plain 药 is what you'd ask for at an everyday pharmacy counter.

components.note: 刃 (blade) pictures something sharp and painful.
心 (heart) below suggests bearing pain in one's heart, giving 忍 its meaning 'to endure.'
爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'

example.hanzi: 他忍受不了这么大的噪音。
example.pinyin: Tā rěnshòu bu liǎo zhème dà de zàoyīn.
example.english: He can't bear such loud noise.
example.fact: 忍受 combines 忍 ("to endure, to restrain oneself") with 受 ("to receive, to undergo") — the same 受 found in 接受 ("to accept") and 感受 ("to feel"), all built around the idea of "taking something in."

components.note: 面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'

example.hanzi: 他每天早上吃面包。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang chī miànbāo.
example.english: He eats bread every morning.
example.fact: 面包 literally means "flour-wrap" (面 flour, 包 to wrap) — a formation that reflects bread's history in China as a foreign-influenced food, distinct from the native steamed 馒头, which is made from similar dough but by a different cooking method.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
亻 (person) — 仅 relates to a person or amount limited to just this much, giving its meaning 'only, merely'
亻 (person) — 仅 relates to a person or amount limited to just this much, giving its meaning 'only, merely'

example.hanzi: 他不仅仅是我的老师,还是我的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā bù jǐnjǐn shì wǒ de lǎoshī, hái shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: He's not just my teacher — he's also my friend.
example.fact: 不仅仅 doubles up the "only, merely" character 仅 for emphasis; it's largely interchangeable with the shorter 不仅, but the reduplicated form adds a bit more rhetorical weight.

meanings: variant of 夥伴|伙伴[huo3 ban4]

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.
亻 (person) — 伴 describes a person accompanying another.
半 (bàn) is an exact match for the sound of 伴.

example.hanzi: 我们是多年的合作伙伴。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì duōnián de hézuò huǒbàn.
example.english: We've been business partners for many years.
example.fact: 伙 is traditionally linked to sharing meals or provisions as a group (as in 伙食, "meals, board") before broadening to mean any close companion or partner — a hint of its origin still visible in words like 伙伴 and 同伙.

components.note: 女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'

example.hanzi: 他带着女友去看电影。
example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe nǚyǒu qù kàn diànyǐng.
example.english: He took his girlfriend to watch a movie.
example.fact: 女友 is a clipped, slightly more written version of the everyday 女朋友 — the two mean the same thing, but 女友 turns up more in writing (news, profiles) than in casual conversation.

components.note: 世 depicts three leaves or shoots on a stem, suggesting continuous growth across generations — giving rise to the meaning 'generation' or 'world.'
纟 (thread) — 纪 relates to organizing threads in order, extended to mean 'record, era'
己 (jǐ) gives a sound close to 纪's reading jì

example.hanzi: 这座建筑建于十九世纪。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiànzhù jiàn yú shíjiǔ shìjì.
example.english: This building was built in the nineteenth century.
example.fact: 纪 also means "to record" or "a period," as in 纪录 ("record"); 世纪 is generally thought to have been standardized as the translation for the Western "century" concept in the late 19th/early 20th century, when the traditional Chinese calendar had no equivalent hundred-year unit.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
广 (shelter) pictures a drying shed.
林-shaped strokes below picture hemp fibers hung to dry, giving 麻 its meaning 'hemp.'

example.hanzi: 这个国家已经把大麻合法化了。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā yǐjīng bǎ dàmá héfǎhuà le.
example.english: This country has already legalized marijuana.
example.fact: 麻 on its own refers to the hemp or flax plant fiber long used in Chinese textiles and rope-making (also seen in 麻布, "hemp cloth/linen") — 大麻 narrows that general "hemp" character to the cannabis plant specifically.

components.note: 比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'

example.hanzi: 比尔是我的美国朋友。
example.pinyin: Bǐ'ěr shì wǒ de Měiguó péngyou.
example.english: Bill is my American friend.
example.fact: 比尔 is a pure sound transliteration with no meaning of its own — 比 ("to compare") and 尔 (an archaic word for "you") are picked only for how they sound, the same method used for names like 比尔·盖茨 (Bill Gates).

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 达's meaning 'to reach, arrive, achieve.'
大 (dà) gives the sound — 达 is pronounced dá, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào

example.hanzi: 他的成绩达到了录取标准。
example.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì dádào le lùqǔ biāozhǔn.
example.english: His grades reached the admission standard.
example.fact: 达到 takes an abstract goal, standard, or level as its object (达到目标, 达到水平) — for arriving somewhere physically, Chinese uses 到达 instead, with the same two characters simply swapped.

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
忄 (heart/mind) — 忆 describes holding something in the mind, memory.
乙 (yǐ) gives a sound close to yì, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 老人喜欢回忆年轻时候的事。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén xǐhuan huíyì niánqīng shíhou de shì.
example.english: Old people like to reminisce about their youth.
example.fact: 回忆 literally means "to circle back to memory" (回 "to return" + 忆 "to remember"), framing memory as something you revisit rather than simply retrieve.

components.note: 阝 (mound, place) shows 邮 relates to stations along a route, the origin of its postal meaning.
由 (yóu) gives the exact sound of 邮.
亻 (person) — 件 relates to a person separating something into parts.
牛 (ox) — dividing an ox into pieces gave 件 its meaning of an individual 'item' or 'piece,' now used as a measure word for objects and matters.

example.hanzi: 我今天收到了一封重要的邮件。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān shōudào le yì fēng zhòngyào de yóujiàn.
example.english: I received an important email today.
example.fact: 邮件 originally meant physical mail carried through the postal-relay system (邮) and was later extended, unchanged, to 电子邮件 ("electronic mail") — in casual speech, 邮件 alone now usually just means email.

meanings: to raise a hand to hit sb

components.note: 力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 别动手,先想想办法。
example.pinyin: Bié dòngshǒu, xiān xiǎngxiang bànfǎ.
example.english: Don't resort to violence — think of a solution first.
example.fact: 动手 covers three related but distinct senses depending on context — starting a task, touching something you shouldn't, or throwing the first punch in a fight.

components.note: 口 (mouths) — 总 pictures many voices.
心 (heart, mind) — many mouths brought together under one mind gave 总 its meaning 'overall' or 'to gather together.'
A stylized foot (related to 止, 'to stop/foot') — originally meant 'to go,' later grammaticalized into a literary possessive/linking particle, similar to 的.

example.hanzi: 总之,这次旅行非常愉快。
example.pinyin: Zǒngzhī, zhè cì lǚxíng fēicháng yúkuài.
example.english: In short, this trip was very enjoyable.
example.fact: 总之 opens a sentence to summarize everything said before it — a cousin to 反正 ("anyway, regardless") and 简而言之 ("to put it briefly"), each adding its own shade of "in conclusion."

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) gives a sound hint — 英 is pronounced yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
讠 (speech) — 语 relates to language, words, and speech
吾 (wú) gives a loose sound connection to 语's reading yǔ

example.hanzi: 她的英语说得很流利。
example.pinyin: Tā de Yīngyǔ shuō de hěn liúlì.
example.english: She speaks English fluently.
example.fact: 英 in 英语 is a phonetic borrowing from "England" (英国), not a native description of the language itself — the same borrowed 英 shows up purely for its sound in 英镑 (pound sterling) and 英尺 (foot, the unit of length).

components.note: Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'
不 (not) — 否 relates directly to negation and denial
口 (kǒu) gives a loose sound connection to 否's reading fǒu

example.hanzi: 请问能否借用一下你的手机?
example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn néng fǒu jièyòng yíxià nǐ de shǒujī?
example.english: Excuse me, would it be possible to borrow your phone for a moment?
example.fact: 能否 is a formal, written equivalent of the spoken 能不能 — 否 alone means "or not," so 能否 literally compresses "can-or-not" into a single word, typical of bureaucratic or written register.

meanings: you can say that again (colloquial agreement)

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

example.hanzi: “今天真冷啊!”“可不!”
example.pinyin: “Jīntiān zhēn lěng a!” “Kěbu!”
example.english: "It's really cold today!" "You said it!"
example.fact: 可不 is a colloquial short form of 可不是 — both exist purely to voice enthusiastic agreement with what someone just said, functioning more like an exclamation than a full sentence.

components.note: 木 (wood) shows 椅 is typically made of wood.
奇 (qí) gives a sound distantly related to yǐ, having drifted apart over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 请坐在这张椅子上。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zuò zài zhè zhāng yǐzi shàng.
example.english: Please sit in this chair.
example.fact: 椅 carries the 木 (wood) component because early chairs were built from timber, and the suffix 子 turns the character into a standard two-syllable noun — the same pattern behind 桌子 (table) and 杯子 (cup).

components.note: A pictograph of an ancient forked weapon, such as a club or shield-tipped spear — the tool image later extended to 干's meanings 'to do, to work' and, in another reading, 'dry.'
氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 工人们正在工地上干活。
example.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài gōngdì shàng gànhuó.
example.english: The workers are working at the construction site.
example.fact: 干活 is a casual, spoken term for manual or physical labor — here 活 means "work, task" (as in 活儿), not its more familiar sense "alive" — giving the phrase an earthier feel than the neutral 工作.

components.note: 革 (leather) shows 鞋 is typically made of leather.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to xié, having drifted apart over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 这双鞋子太小了。
example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xiézi tài xiǎo le.
example.english: This pair of shoes is too small.
example.fact: 鞋 carries the leather radical 革 on its left side, a holdover from when shoes were made primarily of hide, even though most shoes today are cloth, rubber, or plastic.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 周末我们要清理一下车库。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen yào qīnglǐ yíxià chēkù.
example.english: This weekend we need to clean out the garage.
example.fact: 清理 combines 清 ("clear, clean") with 理 ("to sort, to manage") to describe organizing and removing clutter, a step further than 打扫, which is closer to plain "sweeping."

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'

example.hanzi: 这两个答案完全相同。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè dá'àn wánquán xiāngtóng.
example.english: These two answers are exactly the same.
example.fact: 相同 is the formal, written-register counterpart of the everyday 一样 — reports and textbooks favor 相同 (与...相同, 相同的结果), while casual speech reaches for 跟...一样 instead.

components.note: 阝 (hill) — 陛 named the raised stairway leading up to a throne.
坒 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 陛.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 大臣们跪下说:“陛下万岁!”
example.pinyin: Dàchénmen guìxià shuō: “Bìxià wànsuì!”
example.english: The ministers knelt and said, "Long live Your Majesty!"
example.fact: 陛 originally referred to the steps leading up to a throne, so 陛下 literally means "below the steps [of the throne]" — a term of address built, like English "Your Highness," around the speaker's position relative to the monarch rather than a direct name for the ruler.

components.note: 宀 (roof/house) — relates to 完's meaning 'complete, finish,' as in a fully built house.
元 (yuán) was the phonetic base; the pronunciation later shifted to wán, so only a partial rhyme remains today.
十 here relates to completeness, since 十 (ten) is a round, whole number.
比 (bǐ) gives a sound distantly related to bì, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 会议已经完毕,大家可以回家了。
example.pinyin: Huìyì yǐjīng wánbì, dàjiā kěyǐ huí jiā le.
example.english: The meeting has ended — everyone can go home now.
example.fact: 完毕 is a formal way of saying "finished," often heard in announcements or procedural reports ("报告完毕," roughly "over and out") — everyday speech prefers 完了 or 结束.

components.note: 皿 (a vessel) — a chalice or bowl
丿 — a single drop of blood inside the vessel
氵 (water) — 液 names any liquid or fluid.
夜 (yè) gives the sound — an exact match with 液.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了他的血液。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le tā de xuèyè.
example.english: The doctor examined his blood.
example.fact: 血液 is the clinical, formal term for blood (as in 血液类型, "blood type"), while the single character 血 is what everyday speech and compounds like 流血 ("to bleed") normally use.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 大卫每天都去健身房。
example.pinyin: Dàwèi měitiān dōu qù jiànshēnfáng.
example.english: David goes to the gym every day.
example.fact: Like 比尔, 大卫 is a phonetic transliteration of an English name chosen for sound rather than sense — though 卫 ("to guard, to defend") happens to echo the biblical David's role as a warrior-king, a coincidence rather than a deliberate translation.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.
女 (woman) — depicts a wife in the traditional image behind this character.
口 (mouth/words) — the wife following her husband's spoken words gave 如 its meaning of 'as, like, if.'

example.hanzi: 无论如何,我都会支持你。
example.pinyin: Wúlùn rúhé, wǒ dōu huì zhīchí nǐ.
example.english: No matter what, I will support you.
example.fact: 无论如何 belongs to a family of 无论 + question-word constructions (无论谁, 无论什么, 无论怎样) that all mean "no matter ___" — 如何 here means "how," so the literal sense is closer to "regardless of how things turn out."

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
亻 (person) — 佑 describes one person helping or protecting another.
右 (yòu) gives the sound — an exact match with 佑.

example.hanzi: 老人常常祈求神明保佑全家平安。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén chángcháng qíqiú shénmíng bǎoyòu quán jiā píng'ān.
example.english: The elderly often pray to the gods to bless and protect the whole family, keeping everyone safe.
example.fact: 保佑 is used almost exclusively for protection from a divine or supernatural source (gods, ancestors, fate) — for protection by a person, law, or institution, Chinese uses 保护 instead.

components.note: 千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 老师把这句话的重点画了出来。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ zhè jù huà de zhòngdiǎn huà le chūlái.
example.english: The teacher marked the key point of this sentence.
example.fact: 重点 uses the "heavy, important" reading of 重 (zhòng) — the same reading in 重要 ("important") and 严重 ("serious") — not the "repeat" reading chóng; literally, 重点 is "a weighty point."

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 事故发生时,他也在场。
example.pinyin: Shìgù fāshēng shí, tā yě zàichǎng.
example.english: He was also present when the accident happened.
example.fact: 在场 emphasizes physical presence at an event as it actually happens — an eyewitness sense — distinct from 出席, which is used for formally attending a scheduled event like a meeting or ceremony.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 最 pictures something happening under the sun, that is, everywhere.
取 (to take, gather) — combined with the sun above, gathering everything under the sun gave 最 its meaning of 'most' or 'the utmost.'
高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.

example.hanzi: 珠穆朗玛峰是世界上最高的山。
example.pinyin: Zhūmùlǎngmǎ Fēng shì shìjiè shàng zuìgāo de shān.
example.english: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain in the world.
example.fact: 最 is the default superlative prefix in Mandarin and combines freely with almost any adjective — 最高, 最好, 最大 — without the irregular forms English superlatives sometimes need (like "good" becoming "best").

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 他二十八岁就晋升为上尉。
example.pinyin: Tā èrshíbā suì jiù jìnshēng wéi shàngwèi.
example.english: He was promoted to captain at just twenty-eight.
example.fact: 尉 is a rank suffix shared across a tier of junior officer titles — 上尉 (captain), 中尉 (lieutenant), 少尉 (second lieutenant) — with 上/中/少 ("upper/middle/junior") grading the base rank much like "senior/first/second" does for officer titles in English.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud

example.hanzi: 这份合同不可涂改。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn hétong bùkě túgǎi.
example.english: This contract must not be altered.
example.fact: 不可 is the formal, literary counterpart of 不能 or 不要, most often seen in written rules and set idioms — 不可思议 ("inconceivable"), 不可救药 ("incurable, hopeless") — rather than in everyday spoken prohibitions.
